The 'Write-In Biden' campaign, supported by top Democratic leaders and personalities like Ken Burns, aims to ensure New Hampshire's status while still backing Biden. The move has seen mixed reactions, especially with Minnesota Congressman Dean Phillips entering the race, even though he supports many of Biden's policies.

"My activism has been developing my whole life.  Growing up in Henrico, Virginia, I was exposed to the realities of racial inequality and social injustice from a young age.  My family has a deep history of involvement with the NAACP, spanning four generations, which instilled in me a strong sense of duty to fight for civil rights and equality.

Update on homelessness stats in NYC from Data is Plural. Wish we had something similar for San Francisco/Bay Area.

Every night, tens of thousands of people stay in New York City homeless shelters, which are managed by a half-dozen city agencies. Earlier this year, thanks to a 2022 law, the city began publishing monthly statistics on shelter population counts and average lengths of stay, broken down by agency, program, and family composition. One agency, the Department of Homeless Services, publishes some structured daily data, but shares its most comprehensive daily counts as a nightly-overwritten PDF. So Patrick Spauster and Adrian Nesta have built a data pipeline to scrape, archive, and standardize these datasets, and have partnered with City Limits to revamp the publication’s shelter population tracker. In October, more than 143,000 people slept in the city’s shelters, the highest monthly count on record.

🔥A Texas #Rant from a Fighting Sister:
It’s been 3 days since my 15 year old little sister had to travel out of state to receive the #healthcare she so desperately needs. My family is being treated like we’re trying to build a 💣… not access gender affirming care. 
🏥When Dell Children’s Hospital decided to fire ALL pediatric endocrinologists- we weren’t given a warning by the hospital. I was lucky enough to know a whistleblower there who told me to stock up quick because “something BIG was coming for Texas”. I desperately wished they’d be wrong. 
💔But then, SB 14 passed: effectively criminalizing the existence of trans children and the families that ensure they receive medical care. So hopping on a last minute flight to see a new Dr. was the only option. Flight delays have left them stranded- but we’re still one of the lucky few to get this far. 
🔥I’m too scared to post this on places like IG & Twitter…but THIS is the reality of Texas families. And it MUST be brought into the light

OHIO: The Ohio Right to Make Reproductive Decisions Including Abortion Initiative is on the ballot in Ohio as an initiated constitutional amendment on November 7, 2023.

A "yes" vote supports amending the Ohio Constitution to:

establish a state constitutional right to "make and carry out one’s own reproductive decisions," including decisions about abortion, contraception, fertility treatment, miscarriage care, and continuing pregnancy;
prohibit the state of Ohio from interfering with this constitutional right, except when the state demonstrates "that it is using the least restrictive means to advance the individual's health in accordance with widely accepted and evidence-based standards of care;"
allow the state to restrict abortion after fetal viability, defined as "the point in a pregnancy when, in the professional judgment of the pregnant patient's treating physician, the fetus has a significant likelihood of survival outside the uterus with reasonable measures;" and
prohibit the state of Ohio from banning abortion when, in the professional judgment of a physician, an abortion "is necessary to protect the pregnant patient’s life or health."

- Improving our Suggested Followers recommendation engine to suggest people you may already know and people near you.

7dba83bf-f5f1-4e7b-80a9-efc916baf1b2.post_text: I am often asked how I find opportunities to support voting efforts by friends who want to do something but are not sure how to start. I always recommend starting as a VDVR. You get training, you usually work with a partner, and while chatting with the other volunteers you learn about other opportunities. I started by training (one hour) to be a VDVR for Harris County and then volunteered for the Houston League of Women Voters (finding opps on Mobilize), helping staff voter registration drives and education forums at High Schools and community centers. From there I started volunteering for Texas Civil Rights Project doing election help line work at the polls. Last election I worked as an Election poll worker. I have made tons of friends, learned a lot about how my county works, and have gotten to know elected officials. If you want to get started doing VDVR and voting work and have questions lmk.

In the midst of my own battle with COVID-19, I find myself compelled to share my experience in the hopes of raising awareness about the ongoing reality of this virus. The journey has been far from easy - fever spikes that leave you shivering, relentless headaches that seem to throb with your heartbeat, and the shakes that make you feel like you're losing control over your own body. But perhaps the most daunting of all is the shortness of breath, the feeling of gasping for air in a room that once felt so familiar.

This isn't just about me. It's a stark reminder that COVID-19 continues to affect lives around us, silently spreading in our communities. We've come a long way since the pandemic began, but the virus hasn't disappeared. It's easy to feel removed from the situation until it hits close to home.

I urge you not to wait for a personal encounter with the virus to take it seriously.

924a24da-ca37-4d1e-9191-5de2347d104b.post_text: Today my son was at his clinical visit for a 3rd dose in Moderna trial for an Epstein-Barr mRNA vaccine. He enrolled in the trial because he is not 18 and can’t vote (yet) and wants to do what he can to help. Over 90% of people over 35 have had Epstein-Barr AKA mono, and although many of us may not have been very sick, the virus can have long term consequences (inflammation, autoimmune etc). Enrolling in a trial is actually really hard. He has to miss school and make up the work, get his blood drawn a lot, and work clinic visits into a busy HS schedule. The upsides are huge though because we all benefit from safe and effective vaccines. Before covid I didn’t ever consider enrolling in studies - I didn’t even know how. I have done a couple now, and so has my son. You can find studies near you by googling or asking your pharmacist. It’s a real thing to do to help your community. While we were sitting in the clinic today, my Dad texted me the obituary of the pathologist who discovered EB.

Hey Unified!!! I'm going to start posting a lot more here to share insights into grassroots organizing in Texas and to share how folks are coming together with various efforts to improve the grassroots progressive organizing infrastructure. 

A lot of folks have a limited perspective of grassroots organizing. Many will focus on electoral organizing or mobilization efforts. Grassroots Organizing is so much more than that. Mutual Aid, advocacy, activism, and electoral organizing are the major sectors, but it is also about broadening how we measure grassroots organizing. 

Many want only outcome metrics, when organizing is about building trust, relationships, and community. The work to establish these aspects are not easily quantified, but they do take an immense amount of effort, time, subject matter expertise, and creativity. One model that helps people is design thinking. This process model and so many other organizational models start to help focus see the complexity.

A lot of times people don't understand why some grassroots organizers are not motivated to work towards electoral organizing/mobilizing. A big impact for grassroots organizers is the fact that they work on the front lines of the community, meaning where people reside and live. Because of the trauma they experience and/or they see community members experience the prospect of an election solving the issues for community members is just too long and too unreliable. Some Grassroots organizers will emphasize mutual aid work because it's one of the ways that they can directly help communities in the present. Of course, as long as the inequities exist and we don't have systemic change the impact with mutual aid will be limited. This is why so many Grassroots Organizers work in every single sector of organizing because we do need all of it to solve various issues we are seeing. This is also why so many burnout.

Texans Against Gerrymandering (TAG) is an amazing Grassroots Organization founded by Lydia Ozuna. https://www.tagtx.org/

They were created in 2017 & officially became a 501(c)3 in 2019.

As an organization they have evolved their tactics & efforts over the years. As they joined & participated in coalitions like Fair Maps, TERC (Texas Election Reform Coalition), Texas Grassroots Alliance (TGA), & more it became clear to them that they needed to evolve some more.

TGA has been encouraging groups to develop strategic plans through 2030. Last year, I started working with Lydia & TAG more intentionally around building organization sustainability & development. We focused on branding (new logo) funding opportunities, structure, and programming. In January, Daniel Cohen joined me as we met monthly w/ TAG.

Today TAG finished their strategic planning that goes to 2031 and is centered around getting a constitutional amendment for an independent citizen redistricting commission.

Happy 420! 🌿 Today, as many celebrate with laughter and relaxation, it’s also a moment to reflect on the deeper story behind why marijuana was originally criminalized. It’s a complex tale, woven with threads of racial prejudice and misinformation. The history shows us that policies were not just about the plant, but about who was using it—predominantly communities of Latinos and Black men. This racial bias played a significant role in painting marijuana as a dangerous and illegal substance.

As we mark this day, let’s also advocate for justice and push forward conversations about reforming drug policies. It’s not just a celebration—it’s a call to action to correct past wrongs and work towards a future where laws are just and fair for everyone. Let’s use today to educate, discuss, and elevate the voices that can guide us towards better policies. 🌱 #420Day #JusticeReform #HistoryMatters

3. Ask Lawmakers Hard Questions

Ask if they support the Supreme Court’s decision to overturn Roe v. Wade.

Good journalism is always worth it.

Here is one of the simplest examples I can give of why current methods of poll analysis fail basic scientific validity

Consider two independent polls taken at the same time on the same population.

Poll 1 says:
Candidate A: 46%
Candidate B: 44%
Idk: 10%

Poll 2 says:
Candidate A: 44%
Candidate B: 46%
Idk: 10%

Not extremely different, but different. No problem.

Now let's assume the population from which the polls were taken is KNOWN to be:
Candidate A: 45%
Candidate B: 45%
Idk: 10%

No advanced metrics needed here. Those polls are objectively equally as good by any measure. Very accurate.

Here's why the current standards fail:

Consider what would happen if that unexceptional number of 10% undecided split 60-40 in favor of Candidate A.

That would yield a result of:

Candidate A: 51%
Candidate B: 49%

Poll 1 graded as perfect (+2 poll, +2 result)

Poll 2 "off by 4" (-2 poll, +2 result)

Despite being objectively equally accurate

See the problem?

2492b7f1-0ebb-424e-830e-f71f99591d66.post_text:
Ever had the honor of hearing someone say "evolution is just a theory"?

What they're saying is, as they understand it:

1) The word "theory" means "guess" or "hunch"

And

2) In science, it is known as the Theory of Evolution 

Therefore, the Theory of Evolution is just a guess or hunch (and not a fact)

Of course, this statement relies upon a basic misunderstanding of what the word "theory" means in science.

Using a word with two different meanings is called "equivocation"

In this case, it relies on an ignorance (willful or otherwise) of what the word "theory" means in scientific contexts.

While it's problematic that the "general public" would not understand this, no expert - or educated non-expert - would make this mistake.

Well

There's a lot of social science that explains why influencers are not good conduits for encouraging changes in complex behavior. They're great at getting you to adopt simple behavior (try that new restaurant, buy that dress you already wanted). But humans don't trust them when it comes to more complex decisions (what's the best job for me, why should I vote).

One big reason is that most people don't think of influencers as being similar to them. This becomes more true the larger the influencer's following is because the short form video platforms only grow the reach and following of influencers with superficial content. 

So you end up with a catch 22 if you're trying to use influencers to encourage people to vote. The ones with the biggest reach will have the least success relative to their audience size. The ones with less reach will be more successful but will have far fewer people that listen to them.
